paras: The Hyndman circus beating of Black railroad workers took place on the night of August 20, 1900, at Hyndman, Pennsylvania, when William Baldwin, a white former foreman newly made a special policeman, clubbed, kicked and stoned Black laborers while trying to make an arrest. White newspapers reported it as a riot by the workers, under headlines such as "Riotous Negroes."

The laborers, said to come from around Washington and Baltimore, were digging an excavation for the Baltimore and Ohio track, and Baldwin, a Virginian, had until recently been their foreman. Just paid off, the men had gone to a circus in town and were drinking, according to the dispatch.

In the only account, which gives Baldwin's side, one worker insulted him, and as Baldwin tried to arrest him another took Baldwin's pistol from his pocket. Baldwin "felled him with a club, and then kicked him into insensibility," and when the crowd closed in he "disabled seven out of nine." He also knocked out another man's eye with a rock; that man, the dispatch added without naming an accuser, had been "accused of trying to commit assault on a white woman."
That night and the next morning at least a hundred workers marched through the streets demanding Baldwin's blood, and he returned to the scene armed with a Winchester.

Several workers were arrested and jailed on August 21, while the first man struck remained unconscious and "nearly dead." No later report of his fate, of charges against the jailed men, or of any action against Baldwin appears in the coverage.

The story ran as a single Cumberland, Maryland, wire dispatch, printed on August 22 by the Washington Evening Times as "Rioters at a Circus. Colored Men Attack a Special Officer" and by the Alexandria Gazette as "Riotous Negroes." Both opened with the workers having "terrorized" the town and said Baldwin "was too quick" for the man who took his pistol. On August 23 the Fredericksburg Free Lance cut it to one sentence about "Negro rioters" and Baldwin's "vigorous club." No Black-press or local Pennsylvania coverage was found.

reader.title: Hyndman circus beating of Black railroad workers
bases: A newly appointed white special policeman clubbed, kicked and stoned Black railroad workers while trying to make an arrest, leaving one unconscious and several disabled (A1, A2).
All three items reproduce or condense one Cumberland, Md. wire dispatch that gives only the officer's side; no independent local, Black-press or follow-up report was found (A1, A2, A3).

accounts.label: Cumberland wire dispatch (officer's side)
accounts.gist: Drinking workers at a circus provoked Baldwin; one insulted him, another grabbed his pistol, and Baldwin fought off the crowd, disabling seven of nine; the workers then 'terrorized' the town demanding his blood.

accounts.label: Condensed news brief
accounts.gist: 'Negro rioters' terrorized Hyndman and demanded the blood of Special Officer Baldwin, 'who was swinging a vigorous club'.

framing.detail: The Evening Times headlined 'Rioters at a Circus. Colored Men Attack a Special Officer', called the workers 'rioters' who 'terrorized' the town, and stressed that Baldwin 'was too quick'.
The Alexandria Gazette ran the dispatch as 'Riotous Negroes' and added that Baldwin returned to the scene with a Winchester.
The Fredericksburg Free Lance reduced the story to one sentence about 'Negro rioters' and Baldwin's 'vigorous club'.
